analysis.investment_thesis: Bajaj Electricals is a fundamentally mis-sized, overvalued consumer electricals incumbent with zero revenue growth (0.6% CAGR over 9 years) and negative operating margins (-2.1%), trading at a ludicrous 120x P/E — the exact opposite of a SMILE candidate. The post-EPC divestiture transformation narrative has failed to produce earnings momentum, making this a value trap, not a multibagger.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 62.7% — strong skin in the game, above my 50% threshold
OCF positive all 5 years (FY21-25), peaking at ₹914 Cr in FY22 post EPC divestiture
Multi-brand portfolio (Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Nirlep) with durable consumer recognition
key_risks: P/E of 120x on a ₹4,525 Cr market cap — wildly outside my 8-15x entry range for any small/mid-cap
Revenue essentially flat at ₹4,826 Cr in FY25 vs ₹4,590 Cr in FY16 — zero compounding in 9 years
Operating margin turned negative (-2.1%) while D/E sits at 0.85 — profitability and balance sheet both deteriorating
red_flags: Market cap ₹4,525 Cr — 4-5x above my sweet spot maximum of ₹1,000 Cr
P/E 120x — screams value trap, not value discovery
9-year revenue CAGR of just 0.6% — this is a stagnant, commoditizing business
Negative operating margin (-2.1%) means the core business is losing money at the EBIT level
Net profit contracting trend: ₹216 Cr (FY23) → ₹131 Cr (FY24) → ₹133 Cr (FY25) — going nowhere
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bajaj Electricals fails the SMILE test on nearly every dimension. It is far too large (₹4,525 Cr vs my ₹100-1,000 Cr sweet spot), carries zero growth story (0.6% revenue CAGR over 9 years), and trades at 120x trailing earnings — a valuation that demands exceptional growth that the numbers categorically disprove. The post-EPC divestiture (visible in the balance sheet shrinkage from ₹4,993 Cr assets in FY23 to ₹3,833 Cr in FY24) was supposed to be a purity play on consumer products, but operating margins have gone negative (-2.1%) and net profits have halved from their FY23 peak of ₹216 Cr. D/E at 0.85 further tightens the margin of safety.

The forward P/E of 28.75x implies the market is betting on a dramatic earnings recovery, but I see no catalyst. Consumer electricals is a brutally competitive segment with Chinese imports, Havells, Crompton, and Polycab all fighting for share. FCF is declining sharply — from ₹871 Cr in FY22 to ₹318 Cr in FY25. For a Kedia-style multibagger, I need a small, hungry company in the early innings of a massive market. Bajaj Electricals is an 85-year-old brand fighting to stay relevant. Even at half the current price this would not excite me. Avoid completely.
